LanguageData.PastLives_Enabled: Past colonists can appear in the world
LanguageData.PastLives_EventChanceDesc: Rolled once per event: a raid, caravan or visitor group, a quest that brings someone (wanderers, refugees, crashed pods, prisoners to rescue...), a wild man, a cryptosleep casket, the people of a camp or settlement you enter, and per slave for sale. If it succeeds, one pawn of that event becomes a past colonist. Each role below can make this chance higher or lower.
LanguageData.PastLives_LeaderChanceDesc: Rolled whenever a faction gets a new leader, including at world generation. Former ideology leaders and nobles are far more likely to be picked.
LanguageData.PastLives_CooldownDesc: Does not apply to faction leaders or to the return of the dead.
LanguageData.PastLives_MaxWorldLeaders: Max past colonists leading factions at world start: {0}
LanguageData.PastLives_Letters: Send a letter when a past colonist is recognised
LanguageData.PastLives_IncludeChildrenDesc: They come back grown up, with their childhood intact and a new adult life.
LanguageData.PastLives_Role_DeadReturnDesc: Colonists who died in old games come back through their own rare event: as a wanderer, and with Anomaly as a creepjoiner or a shambler.
LanguageData.PastLives_ArchiveStatus: Archive: {0} living and {1} dead colonists from {2} colonies.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Joiner: {PAWN_nameFull}. The name sounds familiar. In another life {PAWN_pronoun} was a colonist of "{COLONY}". Now {PAWN_pronoun} is looking for a new home.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Refugee: Among the refugees is {PAWN_nameFull}, once a colonist of "{COLONY}". Life has uprooted {PAWN_objective} again.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Visitor: {PAWN_nameFull}, who once lived in the colony "{COLONY}", has come to visit with {FACTION}.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Trader: The caravan of {FACTION} is led by {PAWN_nameFull}, once a colonist of "{COLONY}". It seems {PAWN_pronoun} took up trade.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Raider: Among the raiders of {FACTION} is {PAWN_nameFull}. Once {PAWN_pronoun} defended the colony "{COLONY}". Now {PAWN_pronoun} has come for yours.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Slave: Among the slaves for sale is {PAWN_nameFull}, once a colonist of "{COLONY}". Fate can be cruel.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Leader: {FACTION} has a new leader: {PAWN_nameFull}, the very same one who once lived in the colony "{COLONY}".
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Dead_Wanderer: {PAWN_nameFull}. You remember how {PAWN_pronoun} died in the colony "{COLONY}". Yet here {PAWN_pronoun} is, alive, quiet, with a faraway look, as if {PAWN_pronoun} had walked a very long road back.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Dead_CreepJoiner: This stranger looks exactly like {PAWN_nameFull}, who died long ago in the colony "{COLONY}". The same voice, the same habits... but something about {PAWN_objective} is wrong.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Dead_Shambler: Among the shambling dead you recognise {PAWN_nameFull}, who died in the colony "{COLONY}". Death never let {PAWN_objective} go.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_WorldLeaders: This world remembers your past lives. Some of your former colonists now lead factions:
LanguageData.PastLives_MyListDesc: Colonists you saved with the Remember button, files in the list folder, and pawns imported from Pawn Editor and Character Editor.
LanguageData.PastLives_ListWeightDesc: How many times more often pawns from your list are picked than colonists from old saves.
LanguageData.PastLives_OnlyMyListDesc: Old saves are not used; only pawns from your list appear.
LanguageData.PastLives_AllowRepeatsDesc: A pawn from your list can appear in this world again if their previous version here died or is gone.
LanguageData.PastLives_ImportPawnEditor: Use pawns saved in Pawn Editor
LanguageData.PastLives_ImportPawnEditorDesc: Reads pawns saved with Pawn Editor. Pawn Editor itself does not need to be active, only its files.
LanguageData.PastLives_ImportCharacterEditor: Use pawns saved in Character Editor (experimental)
LanguageData.PastLives_ImportCharacterEditorDesc: Reads Character Editor's pawn slots. The slot format is undocumented and may change in new Character Editor versions. Imported pawns are kept on our side and are not lost even if Character Editor loses its list.
LanguageData.PastLives_MyListStatus: My list: {0} remembered, {1} from Pawn Editor, {2} from Character Editor.
LanguageData.PastLives_RememberDesc: Add {PAWN_nameFull} to your list. One day {PAWN_pronoun} may turn up in another world.
LanguageData.PastLives_Inspect_Saved: Past life: one of your saved colonists
LanguageData.PastLives_InspectDead_Saved: Past life: one of your saved colonists, died
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Joiner_Saved: {PAWN_nameFull}. The name sounds familiar: one of your saved colonists. Now {PAWN_pronoun} is looking for a new home.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Refugee_Saved: Among the refugees is {PAWN_nameFull}, one of your saved colonists.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Visitor_Saved: {PAWN_nameFull}, one of your saved colonists, has come to visit with {FACTION}.

LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Slave_Saved: Among the slaves for sale is {PAWN_nameFull}, one of your saved colonists. Fate can be cruel.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Leader_Saved: {FACTION} has a new leader: {PAWN_nameFull}, one of your saved colonists.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Dead_Wanderer_Saved: {PAWN_nameFull}, one of your saved colonists. You remember that {PAWN_pronoun} died. Yet here {PAWN_pronoun} is, quietly looking through you.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Dead_CreepJoiner_Saved: This stranger looks exactly like {PAWN_nameFull}, one of your saved colonists. But something about {PAWN_objective} is wrong.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Dead_Shambler_Saved: Among the shambling dead you recognise {PAWN_nameFull}, one of your saved colonists.
LanguageData.PastLives_ShowRememberButton: Show the Remember button on colonists
LanguageData.PastLives_ShowRememberButtonDesc: Turn off to hide the Remember / Forget button. Your list keeps working; turn it back on when you want to remember someone.
LanguageData.PastLives_StoriesDesc: The "familiar face" letter tells what the past colonist went through since their old colony.
LanguageData.PastLives_HardshipsDesc: Returned colonists bear marks of the years between lives: old healed scars (never lost limbs) and sometimes a new trait that fits who they became. If their story left a mark, the story decides which.
LanguageData.PastLives_ScarChanceDead: Chance of scars for the returned dead: {0}
LanguageData.PastLives_ScarChanceOther: Chance of scars for everyone else: {0}
LanguageData.PastLives_TraitChanceDesc: Added on top of the old traits, picked to fit the role (raiders, slaves, the dead and everyone else each have their own). Skipped if it conflicts or the pawn already has four traits.
LanguageData.PastLives_Role_JoinerDesc: Wanderers, the wanderer with paralytic abasia (Royalty) and joiners who bring a threat with them, such as a refugee being chased.
LanguageData.PastLives_Role_RefugeeDesc: Refugees asking for shelter, and the imperial deserter (Royalty; people who held a title are likelier).
LanguageData.PastLives_Role_VisitorDesc: Visitor groups, lodgers (Royalty; titled people are likelier), beggars (Ideology) and sanguophages (Biotech; only people who were sanguophages themselves).
LanguageData.PastLives_Role_CastawayDesc: Crashed transport pods (also with a baby), the shuttle crash (Royalty) and downed refugees waiting for help.
LanguageData.PastLives_Role_Defender: Inhabitant of a camp or settlement
LanguageData.PastLives_Role_DefenderDesc: Bandit camps, faction settlements, work sites, ancient complexes and other places your people enter. The letter comes when you arrive.
LanguageData.PastLives_Role_PrisonerDesc: Prisoners waiting to be freed from a camp, and prisoners you are asked to hold (Royalty).
LanguageData.PastLives_Role_SleeperDesc: Ancient cryptosleep caskets, friendly or hostile, including those on the first map. The letter comes when the casket opens.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Castaway: {PAWN_nameFull}, once a colonist of "{COLONY}", has fallen out of the sky into your life. Hurt, but alive.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Defender: One face here is familiar: {PAWN_nameFull}, once a colonist of "{COLONY}", now with {FACTION}.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Prisoner: The prisoner is {PAWN_nameFull}, once a colonist of "{COLONY}". Someone has kept {PAWN_objective} under lock for a long time.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Wild: Under the dirt and matted hair you recognise {PAWN_nameFull}, once a colonist of "{COLONY}". It seems {PAWN_pronoun} no longer recognises anyone.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Sleeper: The sleeper in the ancient casket is {PAWN_nameFull}, once a colonist of "{COLONY}". How {PAWN_pronoun} got there is anyone's guess.
LanguageData.PastLives_Letter_Dead_Ghoul: The thing that crawled out of the pod was once {PAWN_nameFull}, who died in the colony "{COLONY}". Someone would not let {PAWN_objective} rest.
